title: Learn When and Where to Connect: Adaptive Virtual Nodes for Dynamic Message Passing on Graphs

problem.claim: Virtual-node-based message passing methods aim to facilitate effective message passing in message passing neural networks.

gap.claim: Existing virtual-node methods constrain all nodes to connect to the same number of virtual nodes, fix connections before message passing, and determine node-to-virtual-node connections independently of other nodes sharing a virtual node.

contributions.claim: MAVN is an end-to-end differentiable message passing neural network framework with unconstrained node-to-virtual-node connections and on-demand virtual-node introduction across layers.

MAVN adaptively determines when to introduce virtual nodes and where to connect them using relative connection importance, selecting virtual nodes through a dual-perspective scoring mechanism over node and virtual-node preferences.
For any node-to-virtual-node connectivity pattern, some MAVN parameter set can simulate that pattern.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on nine real-world datasets reportedly show consistent performance improvements for backbone message passing neural networks.
MAVN reportedly achieves up to 46.5% improvement over the backbone models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing virtual-node methods impose uniformity, fixed timing, and independent connection constraints.
MAVN introduces differentiable, unconstrained, on-demand virtual-node connectivity.
MAVN learns when and where to connect virtual nodes and selects them using joint node and virtual-node preferences.
The authors provide a connectivity-pattern simulation result and report improvements across nine datasets.
